unesco.title: Kochari, traditional group dance
unesco.description: Kochari is a traditional dance that is widely performed throughout Armenia during holidays, festive celebrations, family ceremonies and other social events. It is open to all participants, irrespective of age, gender or social status. Kochari provides a sense of shared identity and solidarity, contributes to the continuity of historical, cultural and ethnic memory, and fosters mutual respect among community members of all ages. It is transmitted through both non-formal and formal means, and is one of the rare traditional dances whose chain of transmission has never been interrupted. Formal means of transmission include the inclusion of a ‘folk song and dance’ course in the curricula of comprehensive schools in Armenia since 2004, educational programmes in youth arts centres, increased visibility of the element through the internet and other media outlets, and institutional initiatives. Folk dance groups have also been active in various communities since the 1960s, and non-governmental organizations regularly hold dance classes. Non-formal transmission occurs within families and through spontaneously formed dance groups. Communities, groups and individuals are actively involved in ensuring the viability of the element, notably through the ‘Our dances and we’ initiative, which has been carried out since 2008, with experienced practitioners playing a key role in safeguarding efforts.

profile.name: Group dance
profile.tagline: Coordinated dance by several people, from circle to line and square formations
profile.insight: In 18th-century Vienna, many couples performed the minuet simultaneously as a group dance in ballrooms.
profile.profile: Group dance involves several people coordinating movements either in unison or complementary parts. Formations include lines, circles, squares, and more complex figures like the quadrille. These dances range from rehearsed choreographies to spontaneous social dances, often fostering social bonds through synchronized movement. Music varies widely, and group dances appear globally in folk, social, and popular contexts.
profile.profile_long:
Group dance is defined by coordinated movement performed by multiple dancers simultaneously, distinguishing it from solo and partner dances where individuals or couples dance independently. The dancers may execute identical steps together or perform complementary parts within a larger pattern. Formations vary widely: line dances have dancers arranged in rows performing repeated sequences in unison, sometimes turning to face new directions; circle dances involve dancers holding hands to form rings, as in the Brazilian ciranda where participants face the center and move collectively around it, allowing new dancers to join by opening the ring. Squares and other geometric patterns appear in dances like the quadrille, which typically features four couples arranged in a square, moving through lines, circles, and figures often directed by a caller. Competitive formation dances involve couples performing routines in unison, creating floor patterns.

Historically, group dances have been integral to social life. In late 18th-century Vienna, the minuet was danced by many couples simultaneously in ballrooms. The quadrille evolved from the French contredanse of the 18th century. Balls often opened with the grand march or polonaise, where lines of couples followed patterns around the room. The German cotillion combined dancing with party games led by a conductor. In modern times, group dances accompany popular songs at events like weddings, with dances such as the Macarena and Cha-Cha Slide offering simple steps for guests. In Italy, balli di gruppo are common at holiday resorts, summer camps, festivals, and beach parties, often danced to Latin-influenced pop music.

Group dances serve social functions beyond entertainment. Research indicates that synchronized dancing enhances social closeness among participants. This effect has been observed in laboratory settings, though real-world dancing may differ. Group dances appear worldwide in folk traditions (circle dance, contra dance, maypole dance), novelty dances (Bunny hop, Chicken Dance), and formation dances (line dance, square dance, rueda de casino).

In terms of cultural respect, group dances are generally inclusive and intended for participation rather than restricted or sacred use. They are practiced by diverse communities globally and continue to evolve with popular culture and social trends.

sections.origins_and_history: Group dance has roots in social and folk traditions worldwide, with documented examples such as the 18th-century Viennese minuet performed by many couples simultaneously in ballrooms. The quadrille developed from the French contredanse, and other forms like the grand march and cotillion were prominent in 19th-century European balls. In the mid-20th century, group dances gained popularity through music industry promotion, with novelty dances like The Twist and Der Ententanz spreading worldwide. Today, group dances are integral to social events, festivals, and recreational settings globally.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Group dances are performed by multiple dancers who coordinate their movements either by repeating the same steps in unison or by performing complementary parts within a larger pattern. Formations include lines, circles, squares, and more complex figures. Dancers may hold hands in circle dances or dance independently in line dances without physical contact. Some group dances involve a caller who announces movements, as in quadrilha. Technique details such as footwork, arm movements, and rhythm vary widely by dance style and are not described in sources.
sections.music_and_instruments: Music for group dances varies widely depending on the cultural context and dance style. It can include folk tunes, popular songs, and specially composed pieces. Instruments are not specified in the sources, but examples include Latin-influenced pop music for Italian balli di gruppo and traditional music for folk dances like ciranda. Some dances have a caller to guide movements in time with the music.
sections.costume_and_setting: Group dances take place in diverse settings including ballrooms, holiday resorts, summer camps, festivals, weddings, and social gatherings. Costumes are not described in the sources and likely vary by cultural context and occasion. The emphasis is on participation and social interaction rather than formal presentation.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Group dances are performed at social events such as balls, weddings, festivals, and parties. They foster social bonds and collective identity through synchronized movement. Some dances serve ceremonial or entertainment purposes. Research shows synchronized dancing increases feelings of social closeness among participants.
sections.notable_figures: Notable figures are not described in the sources for group dance as a broad category.
sections.regional_variants: Regional variants include the Brazilian ciranda and quadrilha, the European quadrille and polonaise, the North American square dance and contra dance, and novelty dances like the Macarena and Cha-Cha Slide. Italian balli di gruppo are popular in resorts and festivals. The rueda de casino is a Cuban circle dance with couples forming a circle.
sections.lineage: Group dance is a subclass of dance involving coordinated movement by multiple dancers. It includes folk, social, and popular dance forms that have evolved over centuries from traditional community dances to modern choreographed routines. The quadrille descends from the French contredanse; many novelty dances emerged in the mid-20th century.

basic_steps: Stand in formation (line, circle, square) with others
Begin with simple repeated step sequence in unison
Use hand holds if in circle formation
Follow a caller if present for movement changes
Turn or change direction as indicated by choreography
teaching.rhythm: Varies by dance; often repetitive and steady to facilitate group coordination
teaching.formation: Lines, circles, squares, or other geometric patterns
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with simple step sequences and formations; advanced dancers may learn complementary parts and complex figures

episode_brief.title_hook: Dancing Together: The Power of Group Dance
episode_brief.logline: Explore how coordinated movement in group dances builds social bonds and spans cultures worldwide.
beats: Open with a ballroom scene in 18th-century Vienna showing the minuet danced by many couples
Show circle dances like the Brazilian ciranda with dancers holding hands
Demonstrate line dances and novelty group dances at a modern wedding
Interview a social scientist about synchrony and social closeness
Feature Italian balli di gruppo at a summer festival
Show a caller directing a quadrilha
Close with a community dance event highlighting inclusion and joy

claims.text: Group dances are generally intended for participation rather than presentation and can be conducted and followed with relative ease.
claims.quote: São danças geralmente intencionadas para participação em vez de apresentação e que pode ser conduzida e seguida com facilidade relativa.

claims.text: Group dances include contradança, dança em linha, dança em roda, and dança em círculo among others.
claims.quote: Alguns tipos de danças coletivas: Contradança... Dança em linha... Dança em roda... Dança em circulo...

claims.text: A group dance is a dance performed by three or more persons together, including groups of individuals or couples.
claims.quote: Ein Gruppentanz ist ein Tanz, der von drei oder mehr Personen gemeinsam getanzt wird.

claims.text: Group dances can be based on choreography with some room for individual interpretation.
claims.quote: Auch Line Dance wird gerne in Gruppen getanzt, wobei dafür eine Choreographie die Basis bildet, die in gewissen Grenzen variiert werden kann.

claims.text: Group dances exist for many centuries, including folkloric circle and line dances worldwide.
claims.quote: I balli di gruppo esistono da molti secoli, come confermano le varie danze folkloristiche eseguite ad esempio in cerchio o in linea.

claims.text: Group dances became widely popular in the 1950s and 1960s due to music industry promotion.
claims.quote: La loro diffusione si fa risalire agli anni cinquanta e sessanta, quando... alcuni artisti pubblicarono dei brani di successo che si prestano a delle semplici coreografie collettive.

claims.text: Group dances are popular at parties and weddings worldwide today.
claims.quote: I balli di gruppo sono oggi popolari in tutto il mondo e vengono tenuti in occasione di feste e matrimoni.

claims.text: Group dances foster social closeness through synchronized movement.
claims.quote: Research reviewed by Bernhard Fink and colleagues found that people who danced in synchrony reported greater social closeness.
